first.rationale: I currently favor simplifying onboarding because onboarding completion is down 4% and activation is down 6%, while prior evidence links shorter onboarding and fewer signup fields to durable activation and faster time-to-value. I will verify the onboarding result and targeted-pricing result before committing, given the competitor’s pricing pressure. The experiment should track qualified pipeline, conversion, retention, and revenue—not just completion—to detect low-quality activation or downstream value dilution.

final.rationale: Run a standard, instrumented onboarding-simplification experiment. The verified result shows shorter onboarding improved completion, time-to-value, and 30-day retention, while prior signup simplification also improved activation. This directly addresses both current declines and is more likely to create sustainable qualified revenue than discounting. Do not use promotional pricing: although it increased qualified revenue initially, retention fell 12% and the cohort failed to survive the first renewal cycle. Measure completion and activation alongside qualified pipeline, conversion, renewal retention, and revenue to guard against low-quality activation.
